Col.name: Col
Col.desc: Stacks blocks vertically. The usual root of a response.

examples.src: root = Col([Title("Delivery status", size: "md"), Text("Three orders left the Bole hub this morning."), Badge("On time", tone: "success", icon: "truck")], gap: 2)

Row.name: Row
Row.desc: Places items side by side and wraps on narrow screens.

wrap.desc: Wrap to new lines when full.

examples.src: root = Row([Badge("Telegram", icon: "send"), Badge("Instagram"), Badge("TikTok"), Badge("Walk-in", variant: "outline")])

Box.name: Box
Box.desc: Groups a few elements with a light boundary when a Card is too heavy.

examples.src: root = Box([Caption("Pickup point"), Text("**Bole Medhanialem**, next to Edna Mall")], background: "sunk", border: false, gap: 1)

Grid.name: Grid
Grid.desc: Equal tiles that reflow to fewer columns on narrow screens.

examples.src: root = Grid([Stat(label: "Orders", value: 412), Stat(label: "Returns", value: 9), Stat(label: "Avg basket", value: 375, format: "currency")], columns: 3)

Card.name: Card
Card.desc: A self-contained unit with an optional header. Base of every dashboard card.

tone.desc: Tints the card to draw attention.

examples.src: root = Card([Text("Your shop crossed ETB 4.8M in Q3, up 11.8% on Q2."), Row([Button("See the breakdown", variant: "soft", onClick: @NewTurn("Break down Q3 revenue by region"))])], title: "Quarter closed", subtitle: "Jul to Sep 2026", icon: "chart")

Tabs.name: Tabs
Tabs.desc: Switches between alternative views of one subject. Tab choice is local UI state.

examples.src: root = Tabs([{label: "Revenue", content: Chart(type: "area", data: data.weekly, x: "week", y: "revenue", format: "currency", height: "sm")}, {label: "Orders", content: Chart(type: "bar", data: data.weekly, x: "week", y: "orders", height: "sm")}])

Accordion.name: Accordion
Accordion.desc: Secondary detail the reader may skip: methods, assumptions, FAQ.

examples.src: root = Accordion([{title: "How is revenue counted?", content: "Paid orders only, net of refunds, in ETB."}, {title: "Which regions are included?", content: "All six regions with at least one delivery in the quarter."}])

Divider.name: Divider
Divider.desc: Separates sections, optionally with a label.

label.desc: Text shown in the middle of the line.

examples.src: root = Col([Text("Paid orders: 12,995"), Divider("Refunds"), Text("2.1% of orders, down from 2.6%")])

Title.name: Title
Title.desc: A heading. Markdown ## compiles to size "lg".

size.desc: xl only for the single headline answer.

examples.src: root = Col([Title("Q3 sales review", size: "xl"), Title("By region", size: "md"), Title("Notes", size: "sm", tone: "muted")], gap: 1)
root = Text("Sidama grew **38%** from July to September, the fastest of any region.", size: "lg")

Caption.name: Caption
Caption.desc: Small supporting text: sources, units, as-of dates.

examples.src: root = Col([Chart(type: "bar", data: data.channels, x: "channel", y: "share", format: "percent", height: "sm"), Caption("Share of Q3 orders by channel. Source: order system, as of 30 Sep 2026.")], gap: 1)

Badge.name: Badge
Badge.desc: A short status or category tag, three words at most.

examples.src: root = Row([Badge("Paid", tone: "success", icon: "check"), Badge("Awaiting pickup", tone: "warning", icon: "clock"), Badge("Refunded", tone: "danger"), Badge("New", variant: "solid", tone: "accent")])

List.name: List
List.desc: Parallel items. Timeline items take {time, text}.

items.desc: Strings, components, or {time, text} for timelines.

examples.src: root = Col([List(["Confirm stock with the Merkato supplier", "Post the restock on Telegram", "Update prices on the website"], kind: "numbered"), List([{time: "09:00", text: "Order placed"}, {time: "11:30", text: "Picked up in Bole"}, {time: "14:10", text: "Delivered"}], kind: "timeline")])

Callout.name: Callout
Callout.desc: The one message the reader must not miss. At most one per response.

examples.src: root = Callout("September figures exclude 41 orders still awaiting payment confirmation.", title: "Partial month", tone: "warning")

Markdown.name: Markdown
Markdown.desc: Rich prose with headings and bullets. Also the fallback when a program cannot compile.

examples.src:
root = Markdown("### What changed
Revenue rose on the back of **Telegram** orders.

- Telegram: 40% of orders
- Instagram: 21%
- TikTok: 15%")

Link.name: Link
Link.desc: A link to an outside page; opens in a new tab.

examples.src: root = Col([Text("Check delivery zones before promising same-day shipping."), Link("Delivery zone map", href: "https://example.com/delivery-zones")], gap: 1)

Code.name: Code
Code.desc: A code or query block with a copy button.

examples.src:
root = Code("SELECT region, SUM(revenue)
FROM orders
WHERE quarter = 'Q3'
GROUP BY region;", language: "sql")

Button.name: Button
Button.desc: Runs an action. @NewTurn is the only action that reaches the model.

examples.src: root = Row([Button("Ask about Sidama", onClick: @NewTurn("Why did Sidama grow so fast?")), Button("Copy total", variant: "outline", icon: "copy", onClick: @Copy("ETB 4,820,000")), Button("Dismiss", variant: "ghost")])

Input.name: Input
Input.desc: Free entry of one value. Prefer Slider for bounded numbers.

examples.src:
$budget = 15000
root = Col([Input($budget, type: "number", label: "Ad budget", suffix: "ETB"), Text("Planned spend: " + @Format($budget, "currency"))])

Select.name: Select
Select.desc: Picks one value from more than five options.

examples.src:
$region = "Oromia"
root = Col([Select($region, options: @Unique(data.sales_by_region, "region"), label: "Region"), Stat(label: $region + " revenue, Q3", value: @Sum(@Filter(data.sales_by_region, "region", $region), "revenue"), format: "currency")])

SegmentedControl.name: SegmentedControl
SegmentedControl.desc: Switches a view among two to five options.

options.desc: Two to five strings or {value, label, icon}.

examples.src:
$period = "Sep"
root = Col([SegmentedControl($period, options: ["Jul", "Aug", "Sep"]), Chart(type: "hbar", data: @Filter(data.sales_by_region, "month", $period), x: "region", y: "revenue", format: "currency")])

Slider.name: Slider
Slider.desc: Explores a bounded number. The best "what if" control.

examples.src:
$guests = 6
root = Col([Slider($guests, min: 2, max: 20, label: "Guests"), Text("Buy " + @Round($guests * 0.35, 1) + " kg of lamb and " + $guests * 2 + " injera.")])

Checkbox.name: Checkbox
Checkbox.desc: Toggles one item on or off.

examples.src:
$forecast = true
root = Col([Checkbox($forecast, label: "Show the October forecast"), $forecast ? Callout("October is projected at ETB 1.71M if September's growth holds.", tone: "info") : Caption("Forecast hidden")])

$vat = false
root = Col([Switch($vat, label: "Include 15% VAT"), Stat(label: "Q3 revenue", value: $vat ? data.kpis.revenue * 1.15 : data.kpis.revenue, format: "currency")])

RadioGroup.name: RadioGroup
RadioGroup.desc: One choice where options need a description.

variant.desc: Cards for plan or style picking.

examples.src:
$plan = "growth"
root = RadioGroup($plan, options: [{value: "starter", label: "Starter", description: "One shop, Telegram orders only"}, {value: "growth", label: "Growth", description: "Three channels and weekly reports"}, {value: "scale", label: "Scale", description: "All channels, daily reports, API access"}], variant: "cards")

Table.name: Table
Table.desc: Exact values across items. Click a header to sort; arrays render as sparklines.

columns.desc: Strings or {field, label, format, align}. Defaults to every field.

examples.src: root = Table(data.top_products, columns: [{field: "name", label: "Product"}, "category", {field: "units", format: "number"}, {field: "revenue", format: "currency"}, {field: "trend", label: "6-week trend"}])

Chart.name: Chart
Chart.desc: The shape of data: trend, ranking, composition. Data comes from a binding, never typed values.

y.desc: Value field, or several for multiple series.

series.desc: Splits rows into series by this field.

format.desc: How numbers display. Percent values are fractions (0.12 = 12%).

legend.desc: Show a legend for multiple series.

examples.label: groupedBar
examples.src: root = Chart(type: "groupedBar", data: data.sales_by_region, x: "region", y: "revenue", series: "month", format: "currency")

examples.label: area
examples.src: root = Chart(type: "area", data: data.weekly, x: "week", y: "revenue", format: "currency", caption: "Weekly paid revenue, Q3")

examples.label: line, two series
examples.src: root = Chart(type: "line", data: data.weekly, x: "week", y: ["revenue", "orders"], format: "compact", height: "sm")

examples.label: stackedBar
examples.src: root = Chart(type: "stackedBar", data: data.sales_by_region, x: "month", y: "orders", series: "region")

examples.label: donut
examples.src: root = Chart(type: "donut", data: data.channels, x: "channel", y: "share", format: "percent")

Stat.name: Stat
Stat.desc: One headline number with an optional change. Building block of KPI cards.

value.desc: The number, from a binding or expression.

format.desc: How numbers display. Percent values are fractions (0.12 = 12%).

prev.desc: Previous value; the change is computed.

delta.desc: Change as a fraction, if already known.

examples.src: root = Grid([Stat(label: "Revenue", value: data.kpis.revenue, prev: data.kpis.revenue_prev, format: "currency", icon: "wallet"), Stat(label: "Refund rate", value: data.kpis.refunds, prev: data.kpis.refunds_prev, format: "percent", goodWhen: "down")], columns: 2)

Progress.name: Progress
Progress.desc: Progress toward a target: quota, budget, completion.

format.desc: Show "value of max" in this format instead of a percentage.

examples.src: root = Col([Progress(data.kpis.revenue, max: 5000000, label: "Q3 revenue target", format: "currency"), Progress(72, label: "Orders delivered same day", tone: "success")])

Sparkline.name: Sparkline
Sparkline.desc: A tiny trend with no axes, for table cells and KPI rows.

examples.src: root = Row([Text("Coffee sales, last 6 weeks"), Sparkline([41, 48, 45, 52, 58, 63], tone: "success")], gap: 3)

KpiCard.name: KpiCard
KpiCard.desc: One number that answers the question, with change and optional target.

format.desc: How numbers display. Percent values are fractions (0.12 = 12%).

target.desc: Adds a progress bar toward this target.

tone.desc: Tints the card to draw attention.

examples.src: root = KpiCard(label: "Q3 revenue", value: data.kpis.revenue, prev: data.kpis.revenue_prev, deltaLabel: "vs Q2", format: "currency", icon: "wallet", target: 5000000, caption: "Paid orders, net of refunds")

MultiKpiCard.name: MultiKpiCard
MultiKpiCard.desc: Two to four related headline numbers read together.

items.desc: {label, value, prev, delta, format, goodWhen}, two to four.

columns.desc: Columns; defaults to the item count.

examples.src: root = MultiKpiCard(title: "Q3 at a glance", items: [{label: "Revenue", value: data.kpis.revenue, prev: data.kpis.revenue_prev, format: "currency"}, {label: "Orders", value: data.kpis.orders, prev: data.kpis.orders_prev}, {label: "Refund rate", value: data.kpis.refunds, prev: data.kpis.refunds_prev, format: "percent", goodWhen: "down"}])

KpiGraphCard.name: KpiGraphCard
KpiGraphCard.desc: A headline number plus the trend that produced it.

format.desc: How numbers display. Percent values are fractions (0.12 = 12%).

examples.src: root = KpiGraphCard(label: "Revenue, last week", value: @Last(data.weekly).revenue, prev: data.weekly[11].revenue, deltaLabel: "vs week 38", format: "currency", data: data.weekly, x: "week", y: "revenue", caption: "Weeks 27 to 39")

ListCard.name: ListCard
ListCard.desc: A short ranked list, sorted by value, with proportional bars.

value.desc: Value field; rows are ranked by it.

valueFormat.desc: How numbers display. Percent values are fractions (0.12 = 12%).

examples.src: root = ListCard(title: "Top products", items: data.top_products, primary: "name", secondary: "category", value: "revenue", valueFormat: "currency", icon: "shopping-bag")

GraphCard.name: GraphCard
GraphCard.desc: A chart in a titled card, when no headline number is needed.

examples.src: root = GraphCard(title: "Orders by channel", subtitle: "Share of Q3 orders", chart: Chart(type: "donut", data: data.channels, x: "channel", y: "share", format: "percent"), caption: "Telegram alone brings in more orders than Instagram and TikTok combined.")

ActionableGraphCard.name: ActionableGraphCard
ActionableGraphCard.desc: A chart the user explores: controls bound to state, plus follow-up actions.

controls.desc: Inputs bound to the state the chart reads.

chart.desc: A Chart whose data reads that state.

examples.src:
$metric = "revenue"
$month = "All"
root = ActionableGraphCard(title: "Regions by " + $metric, controls: [SegmentedControl($metric, options: ["revenue", "orders"]), Select($month, options: ["All", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep"])], chart: Chart(type: "bar", data: @GroupBy(@Filter(data.sales_by_region, "month", $month), "region", $metric), x: "region", y: $metric, format: $metric == "revenue" ? "currency" : "number"), actions: [Button("Explain this chart", variant: "outline", onClick: @NewTurn("Explain " + $metric + " by region for " + $month))])

Icon.name: Icon
Icon.desc: An outline icon for labels and lists.

examples.src: root = Row([Icon("truck"), Icon("map-pin", tone: "accent"), Icon("package"), Icon("coffee", size: "lg", tone: "warning")], gap: 4)

AsyncImage.name: AsyncImage
AsyncImage.desc: The model writes a search query; the server resolves a real image and patches it in.

examples.src: root = AsyncImage("hand-woven Ethiopian netela scarf with a colourful tibeb border on a wooden table", aspectRatio: "5:4", caption: "Netela scarf")

AsyncImageGroup.name: AsyncImageGroup
AsyncImageGroup.desc: Several server-resolved photos as a grid or a scrolling strip.

examples.src: root = AsyncImageGroup(["traditional jebena coffee pot on charcoal", "roasted coffee beans in a clay dish", "small cafe counter in Addis Ababa with wooden stools", "woven mesob basket in warm light"])

Summary.name: Summary
Summary.desc: A short answer up front: one lead sentence and up to four points. Put it first in long answers.

points.desc: Up to four short supporting points.

examples.src: root = Summary("Start on Telegram, then add a website once you pass about 300 orders a month.", points: ["Telegram brings 40% of orders today at no platform cost", "A website pays off when repeat buyers want to browse and reorder", "Keep one product catalogue so both channels stay in sync"])

KeyPoints.name: KeyPoints
KeyPoints.desc: The main takeaways, each with an optional bold title. Numbered only when order matters.

numbered.desc: Number the points when they are ranked or sequential.

examples.label: with titles
examples.src: root = KeyPoints([{title: "Revenue is up.", text: "ETB 4.82M in Q3, 11.8% more than Q2."}, {title: "Growth is spreading.", text: "Sidama and Tigray grew faster than Addis Ababa."}, {title: "Refunds fell.", text: "2.1% of orders, down from 2.6%."}])

examples.label: numbered, two columns
examples.src: root = KeyPoints(["Answer messages within an hour", "Post new stock on Tuesdays", "Confirm delivery by phone", "Ask for a review after delivery"], numbered: true, columns: 2)

IconList.name: IconList
IconList.desc: Points that each belong to a distinct category, marked by an icon and tone.

examples.src: root = IconList([{icon: "truck", title: "Delivery", text: "Same day inside Addis Ababa, 2 to 4 days to regional cities."}, {icon: "wallet", title: "Payment", text: "Mobile money or cash on delivery."}, {icon: "refresh", title: "Returns", text: "Within 7 days if the item is unused.", tone: "warning"}])

NestedList.name: NestedList
NestedList.desc: An outline with sub-points, up to four levels. Items take {text, children}.

examples.src: root = NestedList([{title: "Before launch", children: ["Photograph every product on a plain background", {text: "Write prices in ETB", children: ["Include delivery in the price for Addis Ababa", "Show regional delivery separately"]}]}, {title: "Launch week", children: ["Post three times a day on Telegram", "Pin the price list"]}])

Steps.name: Steps
Steps.desc: An ordered procedure. With checkable on, the reader ticks steps off locally.

checkable.desc: Let the reader mark steps done.

examples.src: root = Steps([{title: "Pack the order", text: "Wrap fragile items like the jebena in two layers."}, {title: "Book the courier", text: "Request pickup before 11:00 for same-day delivery."}, {title: "Send tracking", text: "Message the buyer the rider's name and phone number."}, {title: "Confirm delivery", text: "Call after the drop-off and mark the order complete."}], checkable: true)

Checklist.name: Checklist
Checklist.desc: Items to tick off, with a running count. Ticks are local UI state.

examples.src: root = Checklist(["Restock Yirgacheffe coffee", {text: "Reply to the Hawassa wholesale enquiry", done: true}, "Update the Telegram price list", "Book photos for the new netela range"], title: "This week")

ProsCons.name: ProsCons
ProsCons.desc: Advantages and drawbacks side by side. Stacks on narrow screens.

examples.src: root = ProsCons(pros: ["No setup cost", "Buyers already use it daily", "Easy to answer questions in chat"], cons: ["Hard to browse a large catalogue", "Orders live in chat history", "No built-in checkout"], prosLabel: "Selling on Telegram", consLabel: "Its limits")

BulletColumns.name: BulletColumns
BulletColumns.desc: Two or three titled bullet lists compared side by side.

examples.src: root = BulletColumns([{title: "Telegram", icon: "send", items: ["Fast to start", "Chat-based orders", "Best for repeat buyers"]}, {title: "Website", icon: "layers", items: ["Full catalogue", "Search and filters", "Best for new buyers"]}, {title: "Instagram", icon: "star", items: ["Visual discovery", "Reels drive reach", "Best for apparel"]}])

FactList.name: FactList
FactList.desc: Label and value pairs: specs, key facts, terms. Numbers format like Stat.

layout.desc: Rows for specs, grid for a few headline facts.

examples.label: rows
examples.src: root = FactList([{label: "Product", value: "Yirgacheffe coffee, 1 kg"}, {label: "Roast", value: "Medium"}, {label: "Price", value: 375, format: "currency"}, {label: "Q3 units", value: data.top_products[1].units, note: "Second best seller"}])

examples.label: grid
examples.src: root = FactList([{label: "Regions served", value: 6}, {label: "Top channel", value: "Telegram"}, {label: "Refund rate", value: data.kpis.refunds, format: "percent"}], layout: "grid")

Quote.name: Quote
Quote.desc: A short attributed quotation, under 25 words.

role.desc: Their role or where it was said.

examples.src: root = Quote("I found the scarf on TikTok, but I ordered on Telegram because I could ask about the colours first.", source: "Customer in Adama", role: "Post-purchase survey, September")

Sources.name: Sources
Sources.desc: A numbered list of sources at the end of a researched answer.

examples.src: root = Sources([{title: "Q3 order export", url: "https://example.com/orders-q3", publisher: "Order system"}, {title: "Channel survey, September", url: "https://example.com/survey", publisher: "Internal survey"}])

ChoiceChips.name: ChoiceChips
ChoiceChips.desc: Tappable options for a clarifying question. Unbound, a tap sends the choice to the model; bound to a $variable, it filters locally.

template.desc: Message sent; {choice} is replaced by the pick.

multi.desc: Allow several picks, sent with one button.

value.desc: Optional $variable; makes the chips a local filter instead of sending.

examples.label: sends to the model
examples.src: root = ChoiceChips(question: "Which period should I analyse?", options: ["This month", "Last quarter", "Year to date"], template: "Analyse sales for {choice}")

examples.label: cards, multi-select
examples.src: root = ChoiceChips(question: "What should the investor update cover?", options: [{label: "Revenue", description: "Totals and growth"}, {label: "Regions", description: "Where growth came from"}, {label: "Products", description: "Best and worst sellers"}], multi: true, variant: "cards", template: "Write the investor update covering: {choice}")

examples.label: bound, local filter
examples.src:
$cat = "Apparel"
root = Col([ChoiceChips(options: @Unique(data.top_products, "category"), value: $cat), ListCard(title: $cat + " products", items: @Filter(data.top_products, "category", $cat), primary: "name", value: "revenue", valueFormat: "currency")])

Form.name: Form
Form.desc: Several fields submitted together as one message to the model. Validates required fields first.

fields.desc: {name, label, type: text|number|email|tel|date|select|textarea, options, required, placeholder, suffix, default, wide}.

template.desc: Message sent; {fieldName} is replaced by its value. Defaults to "Label: value" lines.

examples.src: root = Form(title: "Schedule a courier pickup", icon: "truck", fields: [{name: "location", label: "Pickup location", type: "select", options: ["Bole warehouse", "Merkato shop", "Piassa shop"], required: true}, {name: "date", label: "Date", type: "date", required: true}, {name: "parcels", label: "Parcels", type: "number", suffix: "items", required: true}, {name: "phone", label: "Contact phone", type: "tel", placeholder: "09…"}, {name: "notes", label: "Notes for the rider", type: "textarea"}], submitLabel: "Request pickup", template: "Schedule a pickup from {location} on {date} for {parcels} parcels. Contact: {phone}. Notes: {notes}")

ApprovalCard.name: ApprovalCard
ApprovalCard.desc: Human in the loop: the agent shows what it is about to do and waits for Approve, Edit or Cancel.

title.desc: The action, as a short verb phrase.

details.desc: {label, value, format} facts about the action.

preview.desc: The content that will be sent or posted.

editable.desc: Let the user edit the preview before approving.

warning.desc: Consequence to flag, such as "This cannot be undone".

approveMessage.desc: Message sent on approve; {title} is replaced.

examples.src: root = ApprovalCard(title: "Post the restock announcement", action: "Publish to your Telegram channel", icon: "send", details: [{label: "Audience", value: "2,340 subscribers"}, {label: "Scheduled", value: "Now"}, {label: "Products", value: "Netela scarves, Yirgacheffe coffee"}], preview: "New stock just landed: hand-woven netela scarves in six colours and fresh Yirgacheffe coffee. Same-day delivery in Addis Ababa. Reply to order!", warning: "Posts go to every subscriber immediately.", approveLabel: "Post now")

ComparisonTable.name: ComparisonTable
ComparisonTable.desc: Options compared across features. Booleans render as checks and crosses; one column can be recommended.

highlight.desc: Index or name of the recommended column.

examples.src: root = ComparisonTable(columns: [{name: "Starter", subtitle: "ETB 950 / month"}, {name: "Growth", subtitle: "ETB 2,400 / month"}, {name: "Scale", subtitle: "ETB 6,500 / month"}], rows: [{label: "Sales channels", values: ["Telegram", "Up to 3", "Unlimited"]}, {label: "Weekly report", values: [false, true, true]}, {label: "Daily report", values: [false, false, true]}, {label: "Team seats", values: [1, 3, 10]}, {label: "API access", values: [false, false, true]}], highlight: "Growth")

RegionMap.name: RegionMap
RegionMap.desc: Values by Ethiopian region on a tile map, one tile per region. Region names are matched loosely.

format.desc: How numbers display. Percent values are fractions (0.12 = 12%).

legend.desc: Show the ranked list beside the map.

examples.label: all regions
examples.src: root = RegionMap(data: data.customers_by_region, region: "region", value: "customers", caption: "Active customers, Q3.")

examples.label: partial data
examples.src: root = RegionMap(data: @GroupBy(data.sales_by_region, "region", "revenue"), region: "region", value: "revenue", format: "currency")

Sum.desc: Total of a list, or of one field across rows.

Avg.desc: Mean of a list or a field.

Filter.desc: Rows where field equals value. "All" or null keeps every row.

Sort.desc: Rows ordered by a field (default descending).

Top.desc: The n rows with the highest field.

Unique.desc: Distinct values of a field, in first-seen order.

Pluck.desc: One field from every row, as a list.

GroupBy.desc: One row per distinct field, summing valueField.

Round.desc: Rounds to a number of decimal places.

Clamp.desc: Keeps a value inside a range.

Change.desc: Relative change as a fraction: 0.12 means +12%.

Payment.desc: Monthly loan payment; annualRate as a fraction.

Set.desc: Changes a state variable. Runs locally, no model call.

Reset.desc: Puts a variable back to its declared default.

NewTurn.desc: Sends text to the model as a new user message. The only way the UI talks to the model.

OpenUrl.desc: Opens a link in a new tab.

presets.label: Sales dashboard
presets.src:
// Sales review. Every number comes from data.* bindings the server injected.
root = Col([title, intro, kpis, trend, explorer, products, actions])
title = Title("Q3 sales review", size: "lg")
intro = Text("Revenue reached **ETB 4.82M**, up 11.8% on Q2. Addis Ababa still leads, while Sidama grew fastest from July to September.")
kpis = MultiKpiCard(title: "Q3 at a glance", items: [
  {label: "Revenue", value: data.kpis.revenue, prev: data.kpis.revenue_prev, format: "currency"},
  {label: "Orders", value: data.kpis.orders, prev: data.kpis.orders_prev},
  {label: "Avg order", value: data.kpis.aov, prev: data.kpis.aov_prev, format: "currency"},
  {label: "Refund rate", value: data.kpis.refunds, prev: data.kpis.refunds_prev, format: "percent", goodWhen: "down"}
])
trend = KpiGraphCard(label: "Revenue, last week", value: @Last(data.weekly).revenue, prev: data.weekly[11].revenue, format: "currency", deltaLabel: "vs week 38", data: data.weekly, x: "week", y: "revenue", caption: "Weekly paid revenue, weeks 27 to 39")
$metric = "revenue"
$month = "All"
explorer = ActionableGraphCard(title: "Regions by " + $metric, controls: [metricPick, monthPick], chart: regionChart, actions: [explain])
metricPick = SegmentedControl($metric, options: ["revenue", "orders"])
monthPick = Select($month, options: ["All", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep"])
regionChart = Chart(type: $month == "All" ? "stackedBar" : "bar", data: @Filter(data.sales_by_region, "month", $month), x: "region", y: $metric, series: $month == "All" ? "month" : null, format: $metric == "revenue" ? "currency" : "number")
explain = Button("Explain the Sidama jump", variant: "outline", icon: "arrow-right", onClick: @NewTurn("Why did Sidama " + $metric + " grow so fast in Q3?"))
products = ListCard(title: "Top products", items: data.top_products, primary: "name", secondary: "category", value: "revenue", valueFormat: "currency", icon: "shopping-bag")
actions = Row([Button("Draft the investor update", onClick: @NewTurn("Draft a short investor update from this Q3 review")), Button("Copy headline", variant: "ghost", icon: "copy", onClick: @Copy("Q3 revenue ETB 4.82M, up 11.8% on Q2"))])

presets.label: Text explainer
presets.src:
// Text-heavy answer: structured prose instead of a wall of paragraphs.
root = Col([title, summary, facts, compare, tradeoffs, plan, voice, sources])
title = Title("Should you open a website or stay on Telegram?", size: "lg")
summary = Summary("Keep selling on Telegram and build a simple website alongside it, then launch once repeat orders pass about 300 a month.", points: ["Telegram already brings in the largest share of orders", "A website helps new buyers browse the full catalogue", "Run both from one product list so prices never drift"])
facts = FactList([{label: "Orders from Telegram", value: data.channels[0].share, format: "percent"}, {label: "Q3 orders", value: data.kpis.orders}, {label: "Average order", value: data.kpis.aov, format: "currency"}], layout: "grid")
compare = BulletColumns([{title: "Telegram today", icon: "send", items: ["Orders arrive in chat", "Repeat buyers know you", "Catalogue is a pinned post"]}, {title: "With a website", icon: "layers", items: ["Buyers browse and search", "Orders land in one list", "Links work from TikTok and Instagram"]}])
tradeoffs = ProsCons(pros: ["New buyers can find products on their own", {title: "Fewer questions.", text: "Sizes, colours and prices are on the page."}, "Orders are easier to track and report"], cons: ["Hosting and upkeep cost money every month", "Photos and descriptions take time to prepare", "Some buyers will still prefer to chat first"], prosLabel: "Adding a website", consLabel: "What it costs you")
plan = Card([Steps([{title: "Week 1: catalogue", text: "Photograph and price every product in one spreadsheet."}, {title: "Week 2: build", text: "Set up a simple store page with mobile money checkout."}, {title: "Week 3: soft launch", text: "Share the link with your 50 most loyal Telegram buyers."}, {title: "Week 4: go public", text: "Pin the link on Telegram and add it to Instagram and TikTok bios."}], checkable: true)], title: "A four-week plan", icon: "calendar")
voice = Quote("I found the scarf on TikTok, but I ordered on Telegram because I could ask about the colours first.", source: "Customer in Adama", role: "Post-purchase survey, September")
sources = Sources([{title: "Q3 order export", url: "https://example.com/orders-q3", publisher: "Order system"}, {title: "Channel survey, September", url: "https://example.com/survey", publisher: "Internal survey"}])

presets.label: Two-way agent
presets.src:
// Two-way UI: the model asks, compares, and waits for approval before acting.
root = Col([intro, ask, reach, plans, approve, pickup])
intro = Text("Here's where your customers are and what each plan would give you. Pick a period for the deeper analysis, and approve the restock post when it looks right.")
ask = ChoiceChips(question: "Which period should the deeper analysis cover?", options: ["This month", "Last quarter", "Year to date"], template: "Analyse sales for {choice}")
reach = Card([RegionMap(data: data.customers_by_region, region: "region", value: "customers", caption: "Active customers, Q3.")], title: "Where your customers are", icon: "map-pin")
plans = ComparisonTable(columns: [{name: "Starter", subtitle: "ETB 950 / month"}, {name: "Growth", subtitle: "ETB 2,400 / month"}, {name: "Scale", subtitle: "ETB 6,500 / month"}], rows: [{label: "Sales channels", values: ["Telegram", "Up to 3", "Unlimited"]}, {label: "Weekly report", values: [false, true, true]}, {label: "Region breakdown", values: [false, true, true]}, {label: "Team seats", values: [1, 3, 10]}], highlight: "Growth")
approve = ApprovalCard(title: "Post the restock announcement", action: "Publish to your Telegram channel", icon: "send", details: [{label: "Audience", value: "2,340 subscribers"}, {label: "Scheduled", value: "Now"}], preview: "New stock just landed: hand-woven netela scarves in six colours and fresh Yirgacheffe coffee. Same-day delivery in Addis Ababa. Reply to order!", warning: "Posts go to every subscriber immediately.", approveLabel: "Post now")
pickup = Form(title: "Schedule a courier pickup", icon: "truck", fields: [{name: "location", label: "Pickup location", type: "select", options: ["Bole warehouse", "Merkato shop"], required: true}, {name: "date", label: "Date", type: "date", required: true}, {name: "parcels", label: "Parcels", type: "number", required: true}], submitLabel: "Request pickup", template: "Schedule a pickup from {location} on {date} for {parcels} parcels")

presets.label: Plan calculator
presets.src:
// Team plan calculator: state plus derived values. Dragging never calls the model.
root = Card([seats, billing, Divider(), price, note], title: "Team plan estimate", icon: "users")
$seats = 8
$billing = "monthly"
seats = Slider($seats, min: 1, max: 50, label: "Seats")
billing = SegmentedControl($billing, options: ["monthly", "yearly"], label: "Billing")
perSeat = $billing == "yearly" ? 9500 : 950
price = Grid([Stat(label: $billing == "yearly" ? "Per year" : "Per month", value: $seats * perSeat, format: "currency", size: "lg"), Stat(label: "Per seat", value: perSeat, format: "currency")], columns: 2)
note = $billing == "yearly" ? Callout("Yearly billing saves " + @Format($seats * (950 * 12 - 9500), "currency") + " compared with paying monthly.", tone: "success") : Caption("Switch to yearly billing to get two months free.")

presets.label: Bill splitter
presets.src:
// Bill splitter: every number recalculates locally as you drag.
root = Card([totalIn, peopleIn, tipIn, Divider(), result, copyBtn], title: "Split the bill", icon: "wallet")
$total = 2400
$people = 4
$tip = 10
totalIn = Input($total, type: "number", label: "Bill total", suffix: "ETB")
peopleIn = Slider($people, min: 1, max: 12, label: "People")
tipIn = Slider($tip, min: 0, max: 25, step: 5, label: "Tip", suffix: "%")
withTip = $total * (1 + $tip / 100)
each = withTip / $people
result = Grid([Stat(label: "Each pays", value: each, format: "currency", size: "lg"), Stat(label: "Total with tip", value: withTip, format: "currency")], columns: 2)
copyBtn = Button("Copy the split", variant: "outline", icon: "copy", onClick: @Copy("Each of " + $people + " people pays " + @Format(each, "currency")))

presets.label: Moodboard
presets.src:
// Moodboard: images are server-resolved from search queries, never URLs typed by the model.
root = Col([title, intro, photos, palette, next])
title = Title("Cafe interior moodboard")
intro = Text("Warm wood, clay and woven textures, built around a traditional coffee ceremony corner.")
photos = AsyncImageGroup(["traditional jebena coffee pot on charcoal", "woven mesob basket in warm light", "small cafe counter in Addis Ababa with wooden stools", "clay cups on a carved wooden tray"])
palette = Row([Badge("Clay", tone: "warning"), Badge("Forest", tone: "success"), Badge("Charcoal", variant: "outline"), Badge("Linen", tone: "muted")])
$style = "cozy"
next = Card([SegmentedControl($style, options: ["cozy", "modern", "rustic"]), Button("Develop the " + $style + " direction", icon: "arrow-right", onClick: @NewTurn("Develop a " + $style + " cafe interior concept with a coffee ceremony corner"))], title: "Pick a direction")

presets.label: Diagnostics
presets.src:
// Deliberate mistakes. The compiler drops what it cannot validate and keeps the rest.
root = Col([heading, chart, sparkle, stock, tiles, ghost])
heading = Title("Diagnostics demo", size: "md")
chart = Chart(type: "bar", data: data.channels, x: "channel", y: "share", format: "percent", glow: true)
sparkle = Sparkle(text: "Unknown component")
stock = Table(data.inventory)
tiles = Grid([Stat(label: "Orders", value: 412), Stat(label: "Returns", value: "nine")], columns: 7)
